newsitem.title: USA: U.S. shares retreat, drug and tech shrs weaken.
newsitem.headline: U.S. shares retreat, drug and tech shrs weaken.

text.p: Wall Street stocks turned around on Friday morning, dipping to negative territory as technology and drug stocks slipped.
The Dow Jones Industrial Average, which rose at the open, slid 26 points to 8090, amid profit-taking.
The Nasdaq composite, heavily-weighted with technology stocks, lost five points to 1564.

"The market was susceptible to a good deal of profit-taking," Dick Stein, vice president of U.S. Clearing Corp, said. He said drug stocks were weak, hurt by news from Pfizer Inc and Bristol-Myers Squibb Co.
Pfizer stock shed 3-3/4 to 58, after the drug maker said it expected its earnings for the second half of 1997 to grow in single digits over last year's second half.

Bristol lost 1-4/16 to 81-5/16. Norwegian pharmaceuticals group Nycomed SA said a court in the Hague ruled against Bristol's claim of patent infringement against Yew Tree Pharmaceuticals, jointly owned by Nycomed and OPG.
"This market does not take kindly to any bad news," Stein said. "We really could use a pause of sorts."
Technology stocks which had been strong, like Compaq Computer Corp and Dell Computer, also fell.
